findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not match the method signature
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only method with that name, defined in the parent class UsernamePasswordForm, is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` which requires a UserModel parameter. There is no no-arg overload anywhere in the diff. This will not compile, breaking the build for this module (and any module that depends on it).

findings.title: fillContextForm gated on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) incorrectly requires a non-null context user
findings.body: In authenticate(), `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is now only invoked when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, and that helper explicitly requires `user != null`. Previously the fill was done precisely when the user was NOT yet selected (the normal, non-reauthentication login case), guarded only by `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`. With the new gating, on a fresh/initial login (context.getUser() == null) the webauthn/passkeys conditional-UI attributes (challenge, rpId, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI, etc.) will never be populated, so the webauthn form will not be rendered for the ordinary login flow. The same regression occurs in the overridden `challenge(context, error, field)` method a few lines below (previously filled only when `context.getUser() == null`, now filled only when it's non-null), which is invoked from badPasswordHandler/testInvalidUser while context.getUser() is still unset for non-reauthentication flows (context.setUser() is only called later, inside validateUser(), after password validation succeeds). As a result, retrying login via passkeys after an invalid username or invalid password in a normal (non-reauthentication) flow will lose the webauthn UI, contradicting the explanatory comment "setup webauthn data when passkeys enabled" which says nothing about requiring an already-identified user.

findings.title: Unused import left after replacing assertThrows assertions
findings.body: The import `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` is no longer used anywhere in the file after the two `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` calls in passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey were replaced with `MatcherAssert.assertThat(..., Matchers.notNullValue())`. This leaves a dead import that may trigger checkstyle/unused-import failures in CI.

findings.title: Unnecessarily widened visibility of internal auth-note constant to public
findings.body: USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH was widened from protected to public solely so that AuthenticatorUtils (a different package) could reference it via static import. This exposes an internal implementation-detail constant as part of the public API surface of an abstract authenticator class, increasing the risk of external code depending on it and constraining future refactors. A narrower approach (e.g., exposing it through a dedicated accessor method, or moving the shared logic into AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator itself) would avoid broadening the public API.
